verdict.rationale: Otter's pricing page lists "Otter API & Webhooks" and its enterprise launch blog describes a Public API that connects meeting data to any system, so a first-party API exists. Nothing shows which endpoints it has, whether it returns transcripts, summaries and action items, or how keys are issued. The enterprise framing suggests access may be gated rather than self-serve. The OAuth-based MCP server is a separate capability and earns no credit here. Missing for 10: published API reference documentation, self-serve API key issuance, explicit endpoints for transcripts/summaries/action items, coverage of every meeting, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my scripts can pull transcripts, summaries, and action items from every meeting through a documented API with self-serve keys

citations.quote: Custom Integrations with Otter's Public API: Otter meeting data connects to any system, including niche CRMs and proprietary platforms, unlocking advanced AI meeting agent workflows.
Teams can automatically ingest meeting transcripts into internal knowledge bases or trigger actions based on meeting content
